dict.string: Greenroom arranges Google Chrome windows for you (e.g. tiling a new window to half the screen).

Greenroom sends the composited video (your screen with you in it) to the Zoom meeting from inside the app, so it needs the camera the meeting uses. Screenroom records the person presenting straight to a file in Documents/Greenroom, and Greenroom checks which camera you are facing so it can cut between them. Both stay on this Mac.

Your microphone goes to the Zoom meeting, drives the level meter on the participants panel, and is recorded alongside the picture when Marks records a presentation (not in this release; the file stays on this Mac). With Cues turned on (off by default, macOS 26 only), Greenroom also turns your speech into text on this Mac to suggest links; the audio and the text never leave the Mac and are not saved.

With Marks (not in this release), Greenroom turns a recorded presentation into text on this Mac so it can count filler words and pace. It refuses to transcribe at all rather than send the audio to Apple.
